The proposed solution asserts that there exist counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture with one component of degree 6, and that $\deg p \le 5$ is known to guarantee injectivity. 

In reality, no counterexample to the real Jacobian conjecture of degree $\deg p = 6$ (or any degree strictly less than 10) is known to exist; Pinchuk's 1994 counterexample has degrees $(10, 25)$, and determining the minimal degree of a counterexample (as well as whether $\deg p \le k$ guarantees injectivity for $k \ge 4$) remains an open problem. The claimed result and counterexample of degree 6 are fictitious.

VERDICT: REJECT
